Root cause was three compounding issues, not the deadlock/herd problems above:\n4024\t- **`weave` stalled 237s before failing** with the same error `mend`/`unravel`/`knot` hit in 0–63ms in the same cycle, against the same store — something in weave's `bf list --json` path differs from the others and needs its own investigation, plus a bounded timeout so no single strand can stall a whole selection cycle for minutes (`bf-5hlhn`).\n4025\t- **Home-store-missing and genuine failure both report as `error`.** A pure-roam worker (home = no `.beads/`) will always show `pluck`/`mend`/`weave`/`unravel`/`reflect`/`knot` as `error` every cycle by design — indistinguishable from a real bug without grepping raw stderr. Needs a distinct `no_home_store` (or similar) result (`bf-6c8vp`).\n4026\t- **The underlying `bf list`/`bf list --json failed` message recurs historically (07-09, 07-10 stderr logs) against workspaces with genuinely valid stores** (ARMOR, HOOP) — a longer-standing CLI reliability issue independent of the no-home-store case, currently swallowing `bf`/`br`'s real stderr behind a generic wrapper message (`bf-2e4mc`).\n4027\t\n4028\t### 5.5 Testing\n4029\t- Liveness property test: N workers × M workspaces, every ready bead eventually claimed.\n4030\t- Deadlock regression test: candidates in workspace #2 while workspace #1 has only excluded/assigned beads.\n4031\t- CLI-args regression tests pinning explicit `--limit` behavior.\n4032\t\n4033\t### 5.6 Deployment\n4034\t- Version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, then staged fleet rollout through the canary channel (`:testing` → `:stable`). Never overwrite a running binary in place; verify with `needle status` on both hosts.\n4035\t\n4036\t## Exit criteria\n4037\t- The 2026-07-11 scenario reproduced in a test (24 stores, 1 hot store with unclaimable beads) drains completely with 4 workers in minutes, not hours.\n4038\t- A bead flushed into any registered store is claimed without a worker restart and without a 15-minute wait.\n4039\t- `needle status` answers \"when did each workspace last get scanned, and why was nothing claimed\" directly.\n4040\t\n4041\t# Phase 6: Pluck Telemetry Isolation, Fleet Process Tracking, and Concurrent-Dispatch Safety\n4042\t\n4043\t**Status:** planned (ADR-002; §6.5/§6.6 found after ADR-002 was written, not yet their own ADR).\n4044\t\n4045\t**Goal:** stop Pluck's own operational confusion from leaking into a target repo as fabricated work, make `needle stop`/`needle status`/`needle list` trustworthy enough to use during incident response without a manual `ps aux` cross-check, make the fleet's own failure-handling strands (Splice, Unravel) actually catch a worker that's stuck retrying a human-gated bead forever, and make it safe for two workers to share one workspace without racing on git state. Driven by an 8-day incident on `~/ARMOR` (2026-07-06 through 2026-07-14): a Pluck starvation self-diagnostic was written as a bead into ARMOR's own tracker, could never legitimately resolve (its \"fix\" target was NEEDLE's own config, unreachable from ARMOR), and the unresolved loop spiraled into 346 fabricated beads and ~2,300 wasted bead-cycles across two workers over 8 days — one of which (`bravo`) kept running after `needle stop` reported success, and a third (`alpha`) was invisible to `needle status`/`needle list` entirely. Full evidence and rationale in [ADR-002](../adr/002-pluck-telemetry-isolation-and-process-tracking.md). Two same-day follow-up checks found further gaps: why didn't Splice/Unravel stop this class of incident on their own (§6.5), and whether it's actually safe to run two workers in one workspace at all (§6.6).\n4046\t\n4047\t## Changes\n4048\t\n4049\t### 6.1 Pluck telemetry isolation\n4050\t- **Redirect the starvation self-diagnostic to NEEDLE's own telemetry.** `PluckStrand` (`src/strand/pluck.rs`) must never write a bead into the workspace it is scanning. Emit a `pluck.starvation_detected` event through the existing telemetry pipeline instead, with workspace path, open/excluded counts, and candidate exclusion reasons.\n4051\t- **If a persistent record is needed, file it in NEEDLE's own workspace**, never the target's — apply the same isolation rule anywhere else Pluck (or any strand) might be tempted to write its own operational state as a bead in a scanned repo.\n4052\t- **Filter target-repo auto-decomposition for NEEDLE-internal work.** A worker dispatched against a target repo should never be prompted to \"investigate/fix Pluck configuration\" or equivalent — that class of task has no legitimate resolution path from inside the target repo and should be recognized and rejected at decomposition time, not left to spiral.\n4053\t\n4054\t### 6.2 Fleet process tracking\n4055\t- **`needle stop` kills the full process tree.** Parent `needle run` process, its `bash -c` prompt wrapper, and the dispatched `claude` subprocess — not just the tmux registry entry. Verify the PID is actually gone before reporting success.\n4056\t- **`needle status`/`needle list` must have no blind spots.** Every live `needle run --workspace ...` process must be discoverable through standard fleet commands regardless of how it was started (tmux-wrapped or bare background). Add a reconciliation check (registry view vs. `ps aux` process-table view) that WARNs on any unregistered `needle run` process.\n4057\t\n4058\t### 6.5 Splice/Unravel loop-detection gap\n4059\tFound investigating whether the fleet's own failure-handling strands activated during the 2026-07-14 ARMOR (`bf-34xw9`) and Commitgraph (`bf-39by`) retry-storm incidents (both: a worker retrying a human-gated-access bead forever). They didn't — confirmed via telemetry (`bf-34xw9`: 41 `bead.claim.succeeded`, 25 `bead.orphaned`, 42 `agent.completed`, only 1 real `bead.completed`, over 24h) and code review, for three compounding reasons:\n4060\t- **Detector blind spot.** `SpliceStrand::detect_claim_churn` only counts `bead.claim.race_lost` — this pattern is claim-succeeded-then-orphaned-then-reclaimed, a different signal no detector reads. `detect_state_ping_pong` and `detect_log_runaway` both gate on \"no `agent.completed`/`bead.completed` event in the scan window\" as their definition of no-forward-progress; a bead that completes an agent run 42 times without ever closing looks identical to real progress under this check, so both are permanently blind to this exact failure mode.\n4061\t- **Missing config.** `document_failure`/`document_live_loop` silently no-op if `strands.splice.report_workspace` is unset — no bead, just a debug log line. The lab deployment's config has every other strand's section except `splice`'s, so this defaulted to `None` the whole time (confirmed: 455 `strand.evaluated` events fleet-wide in 24h, zero escalation beads created).\n4062\t- **No connection back to the stuck bead.** Even when `document_live_loop` works as designed, it only creates a *new* side-report bead (`[\"worker-loop\", \"human\"]`) in the report workspace — it never labels the original stuck bead itself. Pluck excludes `human`-labeled beads and Unravel only acts on them (§6.1's third bullet); a working Splice detection still wouldn't stop Pluck from redispatching the actual stuck bead, and Unravel would never see it.\n4063\t\n4064\tFix: a new detector for repeated claim+orphan cycles with high completion-without-resolution count; make `report_workspace` a validated, loudly-WARNed-if-missing config value; and have Splice label the *original* bead `human` directly when it detects a live loop, not just file a side report.\n4065\t\n4066\t### 6.6 Bead-Id trailer race under concurrent same-workspace dispatch\n4067\tFound evaluating whether it's safe to dispatch a second worker into `~/NEEDLE` alongside `charlie`, same workspace, same branch. `commit_hook::inject_bead_id_trailer` (`src/commit_hook.rs`) runs `git commit --amend --no-edit --trailer Bead-Id:X` on whatever commit is at HEAD after a successful dispatch. Its only safety check (`src/worker/mod.rs:2079`) is `current_head != pre_dispatch_head` — it never verifies the commit actually at HEAD is the one its own agent produced. Each `needle run` is a fully separate OS process with no lock or mutex between them, so nothing coordinates this across two workers sharing a workspace.\n4068\t\n4069\tRace: worker A commits (HEAD=A1); before A reaches the trailer step, worker B also commits (HEAD=B1, on top of A1); A's check (`current_head(B1) != pre_dispatch_head(base)`) passes, so A amends B1 — rewriting its hash and mislabeling B's actual diff as belonging to bead A. This corrupts HOOP's `bead_commit_index` (the reason this trailer exists at all) and invalidates worker B's own subsequent bookkeeping. Unlike ordinary concurrent edits, this doesn't require the two beads to touch overlapping files — it's a race on *which commit is at HEAD*, not on file content.\n4070\t\n4071\tFix: a short-lived per-workspace advisory lock (e.g. `flock` on `<workspace>/.git/needle-trailer.lock`) held only across the read-HEAD → verify → amend sequence, not the whole dispatch — bounded by the function's existing 10–30s subprocess timeouts, so the throughput cost is negligible. Inside the lock, verify HEAD's commit message actually references this bead's ID (already present per the `fix(needle-XYZ): ...` commit convention) before amending; skip (and log a miss) rather than mislabel someone else's commit if it doesn't match. A further hardening step — swap `--amend` for `git notes add <verified-sha>`, which attaches metadata without rewriting the commit's hash and works even if the target commit is no longer at HEAD — is noted as a bigger, not-yet-required follow-up (HOOP would need to read notes instead of trailers).\n4072\t\n4073\t### 6.7 Testing\n4074\t- Regression test: Pluck starvation detection on a workspace with 0 claimable candidates emits a telemetry event and writes nothing to that workspace's `.beads/`.\n4075\t- Regression test: `needle stop` on a worker mid-dispatch leaves no `needle run` or dispatched-agent process alive (process-table assertion, not just registry-state assertion).\n4076\t- Regression test: a worker started via the non-tmux boot path (bare `NEEDLE_INNER=1` background invocation) still appears in `needle status`/`needle list`.\n4077\t- Regression test: the `bf-34xw9` telemetry shape (41 `claim.succeeded`, 25 `bead.orphaned`, 42 `agent.completed`, 1 `bead.completed`) as fixture input — new detector fires and the original bead gets labeled `human`.\n4078\t- Regression test: two concurrent `inject_bead_id_trailer` calls in the same workspace (simulated racing threads/processes against one repo fixture) never cross-tag each other's commit.\n4079\t\n4080\t### 6.8 Deployment\n4081\t- Version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, then staged fleet rollout through the canary channel (`:testing` → `:stable`).\n4082\t\n4083\t## Exit criteria\n4084\t- A workspace with beads Pluck cannot claim produces zero new beads in that workspace and one telemetry event in NEEDLE's own stream.\n4085\t- `needle stop -i <session>` leaves zero matching `needle run`/dispatched-agent processes in `ps aux`, verified, not assumed.\n4086\t- `needle status`/`needle list` output matches `ps aux | grep 'needle run'` 1:1 on a host with workers started via both the tmux and bare-background paths.\n4087\t- A bead stuck in a claim→orphan→reclaim cycle for N cycles gets labeled `human` automatically and stops being redispatched, without a human having to notice the retry-storm first.\n4088\t- Two workers dispatched concurrently in the same workspace never cross-tag each other's commits with the wrong `Bead-Id` trailer.\n4089\t\n4090\t# Phase 7: Cleanup Command Orphan-Detection Gap\n4091\t\n4092\t**Status:** planned (ADR-003).\n4093\t\n4094\t**Goal:** make `needle cleanup`'s no-flags behavior match its own documentation — remove only sessions with no live process behind them — so an operator (or Claude, acting on an operator's behalf) can run it during incident cleanup without first needing a manual `ps aux` cross-check, the same trust bar §6.2 already set for `needle stop`/`status`/`list`. Driven by a 2026-07-19 incident during lab fleet remediation: bare `needle cleanup` (intended to remove sessions for workers already stopped) instead matched and killed two live sessions — `armor-p6a` (an actively-executing worker, unrelated to the cleanup) and `needle-supervisor` (the fleet's own auto-scaling daemon) — because `cmd_cleanup`'s only actual filter is an identifier-substring match that defaults to matching everything when no identifier is given; despite its help text and doc comment both claiming an \"orphaned sessions only\" check, no liveness check exists anywhere in the implementation. Full evidence and rationale in [ADR-003](../adr/003-cleanup-orphan-detection-gap.md).\n4095\t\n4096\t## Changes\n4097\t\n4098\t### 7.1 Real liveness check as cleanup's default\n4099\t- `cmd_cleanup` (`src/cli/mod.rs`), when called with neither `--all` nor `-i`, must only target sessions with no live process behind them — reuse `scan_needle_processes()` (the same reconciliation helper `cmd_list` already calls, and the one §6.2 commits to building out for `needle status`/`needle list`) rather than the current identifier-substring filter, which matches every session when the identifier is empty.\n4100\t- `--all` keeps its current fully-destructive meaning; update its help text to say so explicitly (\"removes every needle session, including live ones\") rather than relying on a separate design doc to convey the danger.\n4101\t- `-i <pattern>` keeps its current targeted/deliberate meaning (bypasses the liveness check, same as today) — naming a specific session is itself the operator's explicit choice; only the no-flags path's behavior changes.\n4102\t\n4103\t### 7.2 Testing\n4104\t- Regression test: `needle cleanup` with no flags, given one live session and one session with no backing process, removes only the dead one.\n4105\t- Regression test: `needle cleanup` with no flags and zero dead sessions removes nothing and says so, even when live sessions exist.\n4106\t- Regression test: `needle cleanup --all` still removes every session regardless of liveness (unchanged behavior, pinned explicitly so it can't regress silently while fixing the no-flags path).\n4107\t\n4108\t### 7.3 Deployment\n4109\t- Version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, then staged fleet rollout through the canary channel (`:testing` → `:stable`), per the existing convention (§6.8).\n4110\t\n4111\t## Exit criteria\n4112\t- Bare `needle cleanup` on a host with any mix of live and dead needle sessions removes only the dead ones, verified against `ps aux`, not assumed.\n4113\t- `needle cleanup --all`'s own `--help` text states plainly that it removes live sessions too.\n4114\t- The 2026-07-19 incident (bare cleanup killing `armor-p6a` and `needle-supervisor`) is reproduced as a regression-test fixture and does not recur.\n4115\t\n4116\t# Phase 8: Recursive Workspace Discovery as Explore's Default, Static List as Pinning Exception Only\n4117\t\n4118\t**Status:** planned (ADR-004).\n4119\t\n4120\t**Goal:** restore the originally-intended design — `ExploreStrand` recursively discovers every workspace under `workspace_root` (`/home/coding`) by default, and the `explore.workspaces` config list exists only as a deliberate, exceptional override for pinning a specific worker to a fixed set of repos, never as the normal way to populate the fleet's scan scope. Driven by a 2026-07-19/20 finding during lab fleet remediation: `explore.workspaces` in the live config had been populated with a static, 24-entry enumeration of \"all known repos at the time,\" which — per `ExploreStrand::new()`'s own doc comment (\"If `workspaces` is empty, auto-discovers all dirs with `.beads/` under the configured `workspace_root`\") — completely bypasses the real, working `discover_workspaces()` recursive-scan code, since that path only runs when the list is empty. The static list is now stale: `commitgraph` and `twitterapi-proxy` both have real `.beads/` directories but are absent from it, making them permanently invisible to every roaming worker regardless of any other fix. This compounds the already-filed `bf-4df1e` (Explore stops scanning at the first workspace with any candidates) — even once that's fixed, a stale static list still hides whole repos from the scan entirely. Full evidence and rationale in [ADR-004](../adr/004-recursive-workspace-discovery-default.md).\n4121\t\n4122\t## Changes\n4123\t\n4124\t### 8.1 Recursive discovery is the unconditional default\n4125\t- `ExploreStrand::new()` (`src/strand/explore.rs`) must call `discover_workspaces(&config.workspace_root)` as the baseline workspace list whenever `config.workspaces` is not being used for a deliberate pin — not merely \"when the list happens to be empty\" as an incidental side effect of current config state, but as the designed default behavior an operator has to deliberately opt out of, not accidentally fall into.\n4126\t- `config.workspaces`, when explicitly set by an operator, is a **pin/exception list** — scoping a specific worker to a fixed, restricted set of repos for a deliberate operational reason (e.g. a dedicated worker that must never touch anything outside 2-3 sensitive repos). It must remain fully configurable, but must never be treated as required or default fleet-wide configuration, and its presence should not silently disable discovery for every worker that doesn't need pinning.\n4127\t\n4128\t### 8.2 Immediate operational fix (config, not code)\n4129\t- Clear the live lab config's `explore.workspaces` list back to empty. None of its current 24 entries represent a genuine pinning exception — they were simply an enumeration of known repos, which is exactly what `discover_workspaces()` already produces, minus the two it's missing (`commitgraph`, `twitterapi-proxy`).\n4130\t- This can ship independent of the 8.1 code change, since the current code already does the right thing when the list is empty — the bug is entirely that the list was populated with something that should never have been treated as exhaustive, ongoing configuration.\n4131\t\n4132\t### 8.3 Open question: discovery staleness within a worker's lifetime\n4133\t`ExploreStrand::new()`'s own doc comment: \"The workspace list is captured at construction time and never re-read.\" Even with 8.1 fixed, a long-lived worker won't see a brand-new repo created after it started without a restart. Not solved by this phase — flagged for a follow-up decision (e.g. periodic re-discovery on an interval, or accept restart-to-pick-up-new-repos as adequate given workers already cycle relatively often).\n4134\t\n4135\t### 8.4 Testing\n4136\t- Regression test: `ExploreStrand::new()` with an empty `config.workspaces` and a `workspace_root` containing several `.beads/`-having directories produces a worker that scans all of them, not a hardcoded subset.\n4137\t- Regression test: `ExploreStrand::new()` with a non-empty `config.workspaces` (simulating a deliberate pin) scans exactly that list, never falling back to discovery — preserves the exception mechanism's own correctness while fixing the default.\n4138\t- Fixture test reproducing the exact 2026-07-19/20 finding: a `workspace_root` containing `commitgraph` and `twitterapi-proxy` (both with `.beads/`) alongside the other 24 known repos — with an empty `workspaces` config, all 26 are discovered, not just the 24 that happened to be hand-listed.\n4139\t\n4140\t### 8.5 Deployment\n4141\t- Version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, then staged fleet rollout through the canary channel (`:testing` → `:stable`), per the existing convention (§6.8/§7.3).\n4142\t\n4143\t## Exit criteria\n4144\t- A fresh worker with `explore.workspaces` unset (or emptied) discovers every `.beads/`-having directory under `workspace_root`, including `commitgraph` and `twitterapi-proxy`, without any manual list maintenance.\n4145\t- Setting `explore.workspaces` explicitly still restricts a worker to exactly that list — the pin/exception mechanism keeps working for whoever deliberately wants it.\n4146\t- The live lab config no longer carries a stale, exhaustive-looking static list where an empty (discovery-driven) one was intended.\n4147\t\n4148\t# Phase 9: Unify GitHub-Release Upgrade with the Canary-Gated Hot-Reload Channel\n4149\t\n4150\t**Status:** planned (ADR-005).\n4151\t\n4152\t**Goal:** make a new GitHub release reach every live worker on every fleet host automatically, canary-validated, without a human having to remember to SSH into each host and run `needle upgrade`. Driven by a 2026-07-20 finding during the fleet-wide deployed-artifact improvement review: this repo already ships two binary-update mechanisms — the manual, canary-free `needle upgrade` CLI command, and a fully automatic, already-tested, canary-gated hot-reload pipeline that runs inside every worker's own loop every cycle — but the two are structurally disconnected. The automatic pipeline only ever reacts to a `needle-testing` binary written by the (currently disabled) self-modification pipeline; nothing writes a `needle-testing` binary from a GitHub release. Confirmed live on the ex44 host during this review: the installed `needle` binary reported version `0.2.11` while GitHub's latest published release was `v0.2.12`, published the same day — a real, present instance of the gap, not a hypothetical. Full evidence and rationale in [ADR-005](../adr/005-unify-release-upgrade-with-canary-hot-reload.md).\n4153\t\n4154\t## Changes\n4155\t\n4156\t### 9.1 Release-to-`:testing` download step\n4157\t- Add a function alongside `check_for_update()` (`src/upgrade/mod.rs`) that, on finding a newer GitHub release, downloads it to `~/.needle/bin/needle-testing` (the same path the self-modification pipeline already targets) instead of `perform_upgrade()`'s current direct-overwrite-of-`env::current_exe()` behavior. `perform_upgrade()` / `needle upgrade` itself is unchanged — this is an additional path, not a replacement.\n4158\t- Skip the write (and log why) if a `:testing` binary is already present and unpromoted, so a supervisor-driven release check can never clobber an in-flight self-modification candidate mid-canary.\n4159\t\n4160\t### 9.2 Supervisor-driven periodic check\n4161\t- `needle supervise` (`src/supervisor/mod.rs`) gains a poll loop calling the 9.1 function on an interval, new config `supervisor.update_check_interval_secs` (default 21600 / 6h).\n4162\t- Gated behind new config `supervisor.auto_upgrade_check: bool` (default `false`) — independent of `self_modification.enabled`, since a tagged/published release is a different trust level than an agent's own self-edit. Promotion-automatic-vs-manual still reuses the existing `self_modification.auto_promote` flag; no second flag for the same decision.\n4163\t\n4164\t### 9.3 No changes required to propagation\n4165\t- `check_auto_canary()` and `check_hot_reload()` (`src/worker/mod.rs`) already implement canary-gating, promotion, and safe-boundary hot-reload (never mid-dispatch) — confirmed by direct read and existing unit tests (`promote_moves_testing_to_stable`, etc. in `src/canary/mod.rs`). They pick up a release-sourced `:testing` binary with zero modification once 9.1/9.2 land.\n4166\t\n4167\t### 9.4 Testing\n4168\t- Regression test: 9.1's download function, given a mocked newer-release response, writes to `needle-testing` and does not touch the currently-running binary.\n4169\t- Regression test: 9.1's download function, given an already-present unpromoted `needle-testing`, skips the write and logs the skip reason.\n4170\t- Regression test: with `supervisor.auto_upgrade_check: true` and a mocked release, a full poll cycle results in a promoted `:stable` and a subsequent worker-loop hot-reload — exercised against the existing canary-workspace fixtures.\n4171\t- Validation item (not a standard regression test): confirm the existing canary-workspace fixtures (`~/.needle/canary/`) give adequate coverage for a full release-level binary swap, not just source-level self-modification deltas — a real release diff may change more surface (new CLI flags, new default adapters) than the fixtures were built against.\n4172\t\n4173\t### 9.5 Deployment\n4174\t- Ships `auto_upgrade_check: false` by default — prove on one host (ex44) for a full release cycle before flipping the fleet default, per the same \"opt-in, prove on one host first\" discipline already applied to weave/unravel/pulse. Version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, staged rollout through the canary channel (`:testing` → `:stable`), per the existing convention (§6.8/§7.3/§8.5) — this phase's own change set gets promoted through the very mechanism it's building.\n4175\t\n4176\t## Exit criteria\n4177\t- A fresh GitHub release, published while a supervisor daemon is running with `auto_upgrade_check: true`, results in every live worker on that host running the new version within one `update_check_interval_secs` + one canary cycle, with no human action required.\n4178\t- A failing canary against a release-sourced `:testing` binary leaves `:stable` untouched and the fleet running the previous version — a bad release cannot silently propagate.\n4179\t- `needle upgrade` (manual path) continues to work unchanged for fresh installs and single-host immediate upgrades.\n4180\t\n4181\t## ADR-005: 2026-07-20 — Unify the GitHub-Release Upgrade Path with the Canary-Gated Hot-Reload Channel\n4182\t\n4183\t### Context\n4184\t\n4185\tNEEDLE ships two binary-update mechanisms that share vocabulary (`:testing` / `:stable`, \"canary\", \"hot-reload\") but are structurally disconnected — confirmed by direct code read during this review, not assumption:\n4186\t\n4187\t1. **Manual GitHub-release upgrade** — `needle upgrade` (`perform_upgrade()`, `src/upgrade/mod.rs`). Downloads the latest GitHub release and `fs::rename`s it directly over `env::current_exe()` — in place, on whatever host and path the operator happens to be running it from. No canary validation. No fleet propagation: a human must run this on every host individually, and nothing does so automatically.\n4188\t2. **Self-modification canary/hot-reload channel** — `src/canary/mod.rs` plus `check_auto_canary()` / `check_hot_reload()` in `src/worker/mod.rs`. A real, implemented, unit-tested automatic pipeline: every worker's own loop, every cycle, between LOGGING and SELECTING, detects a `~/.needle/bin/needle-testing` binary, canary-validates it against `~/.needle/canary/`, promotes to `needle-stable` on an all-pass (backing up the previous stable to `needle-stable.prev` for rollback), and every live worker on that host `exec()`s into the new binary with `--resume` at its next safe loop boundary — never mid-dispatch. This works today, but is gated behind `self_modification.enabled && self_modification.auto_promote` (both `false` in the live `.needle.yaml`), and — separately from that gate — **nothing anywhere in the codebase ever writes a `needle-testing` binary from a GitHub release.** The only producer of that path today is the self-modification pipeline itself (an agent editing NEEDLE's own source and building it locally).\n4189\t\n4190\tLive evidence gathered during this audit, ex44 host, 2026-07-20: `needle --version` reported `needle 0.2.11`; GitHub's `releases/latest` API reported `v0.2.12`, `published_at: 2026-07-20T12:49:30Z` — published the same day, and never picked up by either existing path. The fleet runs up to `worker.max_workers: 10` per host across at least two hosts (ex44, lab), each worker an independent, long-lived tmux-session loop, deliberately without a central orchestrator (README: \"coordination happens through the shared bead queue\"). Any fix has to preserve that property rather than introduce a controller that pushes commands to hosts.\n4191\t\n4192\t### Decision\n4193\t\n4194\tRoute GitHub releases through the *existing* `:testing` slot instead of building a second, weaker auto-update path: add a download step (reusing `check_for_update()`'s version check) that writes a newer release to `~/.needle/bin/needle-testing`, triggered periodically from `needle supervise` (the fleet daemon that already runs continuously per host, independent of dispatch, and already owns fleet-wide operational decisions like auto-scaling) via a new `supervisor.auto_upgrade_check` flag (default `false`) and `supervisor.update_check_interval_secs` (default 6h). `check_auto_canary()` and `check_hot_reload()` — already running in every worker's loop — pick up a release-sourced `:testing` binary with zero code changes, since they only ever look at file paths and hashes, not provenance. The meta-agent concept sketched above as a \"potential Phase 5\" remains future, unnumbered work.\n\n**Goal:** make multi-workspace roaming (the explore strand) a reliable dispatch path instead of a best-effort one. Driven by the 2026-07-11 lab incident: 24 ready beads across 24 workspaces, 4 roaming workers, throughput of ~1 bead per 40 minutes, with one workspace's unclaimable beads deadlocking the entire scan loop. Full evidence and rationale in [ADR-001](../adr/001-explore-strand-hardening.md).\n\n## Changes\n\n### 5.1 Selection correctness\n- **Claimable-aware candidate filtering.** `ExploreStrand::evaluate` returns at the first workspace with ready candidates, but \"ready\" ignores the worker's exclusion state and unclaimable assignees — a workspace whose candidates are all excluded/assigned traps every worker forever. Feed the worker's exclusion set into `Filters` so the loop advances past workspaces with nothing *claimable by this worker*.\n- **Per-worker scan-order rotation.** Start iteration at `hash(qualified_id) % N`, wrapping around, so workers partition the workspace list instead of converging on the same first store and racing.\n- **Store-layer limit correctness.** The `br ready --json` path passes no `--limit` (default truncation hides low-priority beads); another path passes `--limit 0` (returns nothing on deployed bead-forge 0.2.0). Always pass an explicit large limit; add a boot-time `bf --version` handshake that WARNs on known-bad versions.\n\n### 5.2 Stale-state healing\n- **Mend releases stale assignees on open beads.** Cross-workspace mend only handles orphaned in-progress beads today; an open bead with a dead assignee (e.g. after reopen, which does not clear assignee) is permanently invisible to all workers. Clear assignees with no live heartbeat.\n- **Claim-error ≠ race-lost.** Claim CLI errors currently collapse into `claimed_by=(race)`. Distinguish them; after N consecutive claim errors on one bead, emit an ERROR telemetry event and mark the bead/store suspect instead of silently cycling.\n\n### 5.3 Cadence and liveness\n- **Event-driven wakeups + jittered floor.** Replace the flat idle backoff (observed at 900s) with mtime/inotify watches on each workspace's `.beads/issues.jsonl` plus a jittered 60–120s polling floor. Found-but-excluded is a short-retry case, never idle.\n- **Periodic re-discovery.** The workspace list is captured at boot; re-run discovery every N cycles (or on directory-create events) so new stores don't require worker restarts. The no-upward-traversal constraint stays.\n\n### 5.4 Observability\n- **Per-cycle scan telemetry** (workspaces visited, candidates, exclusion reasons) and a **starvation alarm**: ready beads exist in scanned stores but this worker claimed nothing for X minutes → WARN event; surface last-scan-per-workspace in `needle status`.\n\n### 5.4b Strand-error reliability (found 2026-07-15 dispatching fresh roaming workers)\nThree further gaps, found live: a worker went `EXHAUSTED` with 0 beads claimed despite `explore` finding a real candidate. Root cause was three compounding issues, not the deadlock/herd problems above:\n- **`weave` stalled 237s before failing** with the same error `mend`/`unravel`/`knot` hit in 0–63ms in the same cycle, against the same store — something in weave's `bf list --json` path differs from the others and needs its own investigation, plus a bounded timeout so no single strand can stall a whole selection cycle for minutes (`bf-5hlhn`).\n- **Home-store-missing and genuine failure both report as `error`.** A pure-roam worker (home = no `.beads/`) will always show `pluck`/`mend`/`weave`/`unravel`/`reflect`/`knot` as `error` every cycle by design — indistinguishable from a real bug without grepping raw stderr. Needs a distinct `no_home_store` (or similar) result (`bf-6c8vp`).\n- **The underlying `bf list`/`bf list --json failed` message recurs historically (07-09, 07-10 stderr logs) against workspaces with genuinely valid stores** (ARMOR, HOOP) — a longer-standing CLI reliability issue independent of the no-home-store case, currently swallowing `bf`/`br`'s real stderr behind a generic wrapper message (`bf-2e4mc`).\n\n### 5.5 Testing\n- Liveness property test: N workers × M workspaces, every ready bead eventually claimed.\n- Deadlock regression test: candidates in workspace #2 while workspace #1 has only excluded/assigned beads.\n- CLI-args regression tests pinning explicit `--limit` behavior.\n\n### 5.6 Deployment\n- Version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, then staged fleet rollout through the canary channel (`:testing` → `:stable`). Never overwrite a running binary in place; verify with `needle status` on both hosts.\n\n## Exit criteria\n- The 2026-07-11 scenario reproduced in a test (24 stores, 1 hot store with unclaimable beads) drains completely with 4 workers in minutes, not hours.\n- A bead flushed into any registered store is claimed without a worker restart and without a 15-minute wait.\n- `needle status` answers \"when did each workspace last get scanned, and why was nothing claimed\" directly.\n\n# Phase 6: Pluck Telemetry Isolation, Fleet Process Tracking, and Concurrent-Dispatch Safety\n\n**Status:** planned (ADR-002; §6.5/§6.6 found after ADR-002 was written, not yet their own ADR).\n\n**Goal:** stop Pluck's own operational confusion from leaking into a target repo as fabricated work, make `needle stop`/`needle status`/`needle list` trustworthy enough to use during incident response without a manual `ps aux` cross-check, make the fleet's own failure-handling strands (Splice, Unravel) actually catch a worker that's stuck retrying a human-gated bead forever, and make it safe for two workers to share one workspace without racing on git state. Driven by an 8-day incident on `~/ARMOR` (2026-07-06 through 2026-07-14): a Pluck starvation self-diagnostic was written as a bead into ARMOR's own tracker, could never legitimately resolve (its \"fix\" target was NEEDLE's own config, unreachable from ARMOR), and the unresolved loop spiraled into 346 fabricated beads and ~2,300 wasted bead-cycles across two workers over 8 days — one of which (`bravo`) kept running after `needle stop` reported success, and a third (`alpha`) was invisible to `needle status`/`needle list` entirely. Full evidence and rationale in [ADR-002](../adr/002-pluck-telemetry-isolation-and-process-tracking.md). Two same-day follow-up checks found further gaps: why didn't Splice/Unravel stop this class of incident on their own (§6.5), and whether it's actually safe to run two workers in one workspace at all (§6.6).\n\n## Changes\n\n### 6.1 Pluck telemetry isolation\n- **Redirect the starvation self-diagnostic to NEEDLE's own telemetry.** `PluckStrand` (`src/strand/pluck.rs`) must never write a bead into the workspace it is scanning. Emit a `pluck.starvation_detected` event through the existing telemetry pipeline instead, with workspace path, open/excluded counts, and candidate exclusion reasons.\n- **If a persistent record is needed, file it in NEEDLE's own workspace**, never the target's — apply the same isolation rule anywhere else Pluck (or any strand) might be tempted to write its own operational state as a bead in a scanned repo.\n- **Filter target-repo auto-decomposition for NEEDLE-internal work.** A worker dispatched against a target repo should never be prompted to \"investigate/fix Pluck configuration\" or equivalent — that class of task has no legitimate resolution path from inside the target repo and should be recognized and rejected at decomposition time, not left to spiral.\n\n### 6.2 Fleet process tracking\n- **`needle stop` kills the full process tree.** Parent `needle run` process, its `bash -c` prompt wrapper, and the dispatched `claude` subprocess — not just the tmux registry entry. Verify the PID is actually gone before reporting success.\n- **`needle status`/`needle list` must have no blind spots.** Every live `needle run --workspace ...` process must be discoverable through standard fleet commands regardless of how it was started (tmux-wrapped or bare background). Add a reconciliation check (registry view vs. `ps aux` process-table view) that WARNs on any unregistered `needle run` process.\n\n### 6.5 Splice/Unravel loop-detection gap\nFound investigating whether the fleet's own failure-handling strands activated during the 2026-07-14 ARMOR (`bf-34xw9`) and Commitgraph (`bf-39by`) retry-storm incidents (both: a worker retrying a human-gated-access bead forever). They didn't — confirmed via telemetry (`bf-34xw9`: 41 `bead.claim.succeeded`, 25 `bead.orphaned`, 42 `agent.completed`, only 1 real `bead.completed`, over 24h) and code review, for three compounding reasons:\n- **Detector blind spot.** `SpliceStrand::detect_claim_churn` only counts `bead.claim.race_lost` — this pattern is claim-succeeded-then-orphaned-then-reclaimed, a different signal no detector reads. `detect_state_ping_pong` and `detect_log_runaway` both gate on \"no `agent.completed`/`bead.completed` event in the scan window\" as their definition of no-forward-progress; a bead that completes an agent run 42 times without ever closing looks identical to real progress under this check, so both are permanently blind to this exact failure mode.\n- **Missing config.** `document_failure`/`document_live_loop` silently no-op if `strands.splice.report_workspace` is unset — no bead, just a debug log line. The lab deployment's config has every other strand's section except `splice`'s, so this defaulted to `None` the whole time (confirmed: 455 `strand.evaluated` events fleet-wide in 24h, zero escalation beads created).\n- **No connection back to the stuck bead.** Even when `document_live_loop` works as designed, it only creates a *new* side-report bead (`[\"worker-loop\", \"human\"]`) in the report workspace — it never labels the original stuck bead itself. Pluck excludes `human`-labeled beads and Unravel only acts on them (§6.1's third bullet); a working Splice detection still wouldn't stop Pluck from redispatching the actual stuck bead, and Unravel would never see it.\n\nFix: a new detector for repeated claim+orphan cycles with high completion-without-resolution count; make `report_workspace` a validated, loudly-WARNed-if-missing config value; and have Splice label the *original* bead `human` directly when it detects a live loop, not just file a side report.\n\n### 6.6 Bead-Id trailer race under concurrent same-workspace dispatch\nFound evaluating whether it's safe to dispatch a second worker into `~/NEEDLE` alongside `charlie`, same workspace, same branch. `commit_hook::inject_bead_id_trailer` (`src/commit_hook.rs`) runs `git commit --amend --no-edit --trailer Bead-Id:X` on whatever commit is at HEAD after a successful dispatch. Its only safety check (`src/worker/mod.rs:2079`) is `current_head != pre_dispatch_head` — it never verifies the commit actually at HEAD is the one its own agent produced. Each `needle run` is a fully separate OS process with no lock or mutex between them, so nothing coordinates this across two workers sharing a workspace.\n\nRace: worker A commits (HEAD=A1); before A reaches the trailer step, worker B also commits (HEAD=B1, on top of A1); A's check (`current_head(B1) != pre_dispatch_head(base)`) passes, so A amends B1 — rewriting its hash and mislabeling B's actual diff as belonging to bead A. This corrupts HOOP's `bead_commit_index` (the reason this trailer exists at all) and invalidates worker B's own subsequent bookkeeping. Unlike ordinary concurrent edits, this doesn't require the two beads to touch overlapping files — it's a race on *which commit is at HEAD*, not on file content.\n\nFix: a short-lived per-workspace advisory lock (e.g. `flock` on `<workspace>/.git/needle-trailer.lock`) held only across the read-HEAD → verify → amend sequence, not the whole dispatch — bounded by the function's existing 10–30s subprocess timeouts, so the throughput cost is negligible. Inside the lock, verify HEAD's commit message actually references this bead's ID (already present per the `fix(needle-XYZ): ...` commit convention) before amending; skip (and log a miss) rather than mislabel someone else's commit if it doesn't match. A further hardening step — swap `--amend` for `git notes add <verified-sha>`, which attaches metadata without rewriting the commit's hash and works even if the target commit is no longer at HEAD — is noted as a bigger, not-yet-required follow-up (HOOP would need to read notes instead of trailers).\n\n### 6.7 Testing\n- Regression test: Pluck starvation detection on a workspace with 0 claimable candidates emits a telemetry event and writes nothing to that workspace's `.beads/`.\n- Regression test: `needle stop` on a worker mid-dispatch leaves no `needle run` or dispatched-agent process alive (process-table assertion, not just registry-state assertion).\n- Regression test: a worker started via the non-tmux boot path (bare `NEEDLE_INNER=1` background invocation) still appears in `needle status`/`needle list`.\n- Regression test: the `bf-34xw9` telemetry shape (41 `claim.succeeded`, 25 `bead.orphaned`, 42 `agent.completed`, 1 `bead.completed`) as fixture input — new detector fires and the original bead gets labeled `human`.\n- Regression test: two concurrent `inject_bead_id_trailer` calls in the same workspace (simulated racing threads/processes against one repo fixture) never cross-tag each other's commit.\n\n### 6.8 Deployment\n- Version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, then staged fleet rollout through the canary channel (`:testing` → `:stable`).\n\n## Exit criteria\n- A workspace with beads Pluck cannot claim produces zero new beads in that workspace and one telemetry event in NEEDLE's own stream.\n- `needle stop -i <session>` leaves zero matching `needle run`/dispatched-agent processes in `ps aux`, verified, not assumed.\n- `needle status`/`needle list` output matches `ps aux | grep 'needle run'` 1:1 on a host with workers started via both the tmux and bare-background paths.\n- A bead stuck in a claim→orphan→reclaim cycle for N cycles gets labeled `human` automatically and stops being redispatched, without a human having to notice the retry-storm first.\n- Two workers dispatched concurrently in the same workspace never cross-tag each other's commits with the wrong `Bead-Id` trailer.\n\n# Phase 7: Cleanup Command Orphan-Detection Gap\n\n**Status:** planned (ADR-003).\n\n**Goal:** make `needle cleanup`'s no-flags behavior match its own documentation — remove only sessions with no live process behind them — so an operator (or Claude, acting on an operator's behalf) can run it during incident cleanup without first needing a manual `ps aux` cross-check, the same trust bar §6.2 already set for `needle stop`/`status`/`list`. Driven by a 2026-07-19 incident during lab fleet remediation: bare `needle cleanup` (intended to remove sessions for workers already stopped) instead matched and killed two live sessions — `armor-p6a` (an actively-executing worker, unrelated to the cleanup) and `needle-supervisor` (the fleet's own auto-scaling daemon) — because `cmd_cleanup`'s only actual filter is an identifier-substring match that defaults to matching everything when no identifier is given; despite its help text and doc comment both claiming an \"orphaned sessions only\" check, no liveness check exists anywhere in the implementation. Full evidence and rationale in [ADR-003](../adr/003-cleanup-orphan-detection-gap.md).\n\n## Changes\n\n### 7.1 Real liveness check as cleanup's default\n- `cmd_cleanup` (`src/cli/mod.rs`), when called with neither `--all` nor `-i`, must only target sessions with no live process behind them — reuse `scan_needle_processes()` (the same reconciliation helper `cmd_list` already calls, and the one §6.2 commits to building out for `needle status`/`needle list`) rather than the current identifier-substring filter, which matches every session when the identifier is empty.\n- `--all` keeps its current fully-destructive meaning; update its help text to say so explicitly (\"removes every needle session, including live ones\") rather than relying on a separate design doc to convey the danger.\n- `-i <pattern>` keeps its current targeted/deliberate meaning (bypasses the liveness check, same as today) — naming a specific session is itself the operator's explicit choice; only the no-flags path's behavior changes.\n\n### 7.2 Testing\n- Regression test: `needle cleanup` with no flags, given one live session and one session with no backing process, removes only the dead one.\n- Regression test: `needle cleanup` with no flags and zero dead sessions removes nothing and says so, even when live sessions exist.\n- Regression test: `needle cleanup --all` still removes every session regardless of liveness (unchanged behavior, pinned explicitly so it can't regress silently while fixing the no-flags path).\n\n### 7.3 Deployment\n- Version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, then staged fleet rollout through the canary channel (`:testing` → `:stable`), per the existing convention (§6.8).\n\n## Exit criteria\n- Bare `needle cleanup` on a host with any mix of live and dead needle sessions removes only the dead ones, verified against `ps aux`, not assumed.\n- `needle cleanup --all`'s own `--help` text states plainly that it removes live sessions too.\n- The 2026-07-19 incident (bare cleanup killing `armor-p6a` and `needle-supervisor`) is reproduced as a regression-test fixture and does not recur.\n\n# Phase 8: Recursive Workspace Discovery as Explore's Default, Static List as Pinning Exception Only\n\n**Status:** planned (ADR-004).\n\n**Goal:** restore the originally-intended design — `ExploreStrand` recursively discovers every workspace under `workspace_root` (`/home/coding`) by default, and the `explore.workspaces` config list exists only as a deliberate, exceptional override for pinning a specific worker to a fixed set of repos, never as the normal way to populate the fleet's scan scope. Driven by a 2026-07-19/20 finding during lab fleet remediation: `explore.workspaces` in the live config had been populated with a static, 24-entry enumeration of \"all known repos at the time,\" which — per `ExploreStrand::new()`'s own doc comment (\"If `workspaces` is empty, auto-discovers all dirs with `.beads/` under the configured `workspace_root`\") — completely bypasses the real, working `discover_workspaces()` recursive-scan code, since that path only runs when the list is empty. The static list is now stale: `commitgraph` and `twitterapi-proxy` both have real `.beads/` directories but are absent from it, making them permanently invisible to every roaming worker regardless of any other fix. This compounds the already-filed `bf-4df1e` (Explore stops scanning at the first workspace with any candidates) — even once that's fixed, a stale static list still hides whole repos from the scan entirely. Full evidence and rationale in [ADR-004](../adr/004-recursive-workspace-discovery-default.md).\n\n## Changes\n\n### 8.1 Recursive discovery is the unconditional default\n- `ExploreStrand::new()` (`src/strand/explore.rs`) must call `discover_workspaces(&config.workspace_root)` as the baseline workspace list whenever `config.workspaces` is not being used for a deliberate pin — not merely \"when the list happens to be empty\" as an incidental side effect of current config state, but as the designed default behavior an operator has to deliberately opt out of, not accidentally fall into.\n- `config.workspaces`, when explicitly set by an operator, is a **pin/exception list** — scoping a specific worker to a fixed, restricted set of repos for a deliberate operational reason (e.g. a dedicated worker that must never touch anything outside 2-3 sensitive repos). It must remain fully configurable, but must never be treated as required or default fleet-wide configuration, and its presence should not silently disable discovery for every worker that doesn't need pinning.\n\n### 8.2 Immediate operational fix (config, not code)\n- Clear the live lab config's `explore.workspaces` list back to empty. None of its current 24 entries represent a genuine pinning exception — they were simply an enumeration of known repos, which is exactly what `discover_workspaces()` already produces, minus the two it's missing (`commitgraph`, `twitterapi-proxy`).\n- This can ship independent of the 8.1 code change, since the current code already does the right thing when the list is empty — the bug is entirely that the list was populated with something that should never have been treated as exhaustive, ongoing configuration.\n\n### 8.3 Open question: discovery staleness within a worker's lifetime\n`ExploreStrand::new()`'s own doc comment: \"The workspace list is captured at construction time and never re-read.\" Even with 8.1 fixed, a long-lived worker won't see a brand-new repo created after it started without a restart. Not solved by this phase — flagged for a follow-up decision (e.g. periodic re-discovery on an interval, or accept restart-to-pick-up-new-repos as adequate given workers already cycle relatively often).\n\n### 8.4 Testing\n- Regression test: `ExploreStrand::new()` with an empty `config.workspaces` and a `workspace_root` containing several `.beads/`-having directories produces a worker that scans all of them, not a hardcoded subset.\n- Regression test: `ExploreStrand::new()` with a non-empty `config.workspaces` (simulating a deliberate pin) scans exactly that list, never falling back to discovery — preserves the exception mechanism's own correctness while fixing the default.\n- Fixture test reproducing the exact 2026-07-19/20 finding: a `workspace_root` containing `commitgraph` and `twitterapi-proxy` (both with `.beads/`) alongside the other 24 known repos — with an empty `workspaces` config, all 26 are discovered, not just the 24 that happened to be hand-listed.\n\n### 8.5 Deployment\n- Version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, then staged fleet rollout through the canary channel (`:testing` → `:stable`), per the existing convention (§6.8/§7.3).\n\n## Exit criteria\n- A fresh worker with `explore.workspaces` unset (or emptied) discovers every `.beads/`-having directory under `workspace_root`, including `commitgraph` and `twitterapi-proxy`, without any manual list maintenance.\n- Setting `explore.workspaces` explicitly still restricts a worker to exactly that list — the pin/exception mechanism keeps working for whoever deliberately wants it.\n- The live lab config no longer carries a stale, exhaustive-looking static list where an empty (discovery-driven) one was intended.\n\n# Phase 9: Unify GitHub-Release Upgrade with the Canary-Gated Hot-Reload Channel\n\n**Status:** planned (ADR-005).\n\n**Goal:** make a new GitHub release reach every live worker on every fleet host automatically, canary-validated, without a human having to remember to SSH into each host and run `needle upgrade`. Driven by a 2026-07-20 finding during the fleet-wide deployed-artifact improvement review: this repo already ships two binary-update mechanisms — the manual, canary-free `needle upgrade` CLI command, and a fully automatic, already-tested, canary-gated hot-reload pipeline that runs inside every worker's own loop every cycle — but the two are structurally disconnected. The automatic pipeline only ever reacts to a `needle-testing` binary written by the (currently disabled) self-modification pipeline; nothing writes a `needle-testing` binary from a GitHub release. Confirmed live on the ex44 host during this review: the installed `needle` binary reported version `0.2.11` while GitHub's latest published release was `v0.2.12`, published the same day — a real, present instance of the gap, not a hypothetical. Full evidence and rationale in [ADR-005](../adr/005-unify-release-upgrade-with-canary-hot-reload.md).\n\n## Changes\n\n### 9.1 Release-to-`:testing` download step\n- Add a function alongside `check_for_update()` (`src/upgrade/mod.rs`) that, on finding a newer GitHub release, downloads it to `~/.needle/bin/needle-testing` (the same path the self-modification pipeline already targets) instead of `perform_upgrade()`'s current direct-overwrite-of-`env::current_exe()` behavior. `perform_upgrade()` / `needle upgrade` itself is unchanged — this is an additional path, not a replacement.\n- Skip the write (and log why) if a `:testing` binary is already present and unpromoted, so a supervisor-driven release check can never clobber an in-flight self-modification candidate mid-canary.\n\n### 9.2 Supervisor-driven periodic check\n- `needle supervise` (`src/supervisor/mod.rs`) gains a poll loop calling the 9.1 function on an interval, new config `supervisor.update_check_interval_secs` (default 21600 / 6h).\n- Gated behind new config `supervisor.auto_upgrade_check: bool` (default `false`) — independent of `self_modification.enabled`, since a tagged/published release is a different trust level than an agent's own self-edit. Promotion-automatic-vs-manual still reuses the existing `self_modification.auto_promote` flag; no second flag for the same decision.\n\n### 9.3 No changes required to propagation\n- `check_auto_canary()` and `check_hot_reload()` (`src/worker/mod.rs`) already implement canary-gating, promotion, and safe-boundary hot-reload (never mid-dispatch) — confirmed by direct read and existing unit tests (`promote_moves_testing_to_stable`, etc. in `src/canary/mod.rs`). They pick up a release-sourced `:testing` binary with zero modification once 9.1/9.2 land.\n\n### 9.4 Testing\n- Regression test: 9.1's download function, given a mocked newer-release response, writes to `needle-testing` and does not touch the currently-running binary.\n- Regression test: 9.1's download function, given an already-present unpromoted `needle-testing`, skips the write and logs the skip reason.\n- Regression test: with `supervisor.auto_upgrade_check: true` and a mocked release, a full poll cycle results in a promoted `:stable` and a subsequent worker-loop hot-reload — exercised against the existing canary-workspace fixtures.\n- Validation item (not a standard regression test): confirm the existing canary-workspace fixtures (`~/.needle/canary/`) give adequate coverage for a full release-level binary swap, not just source-level self-modification deltas — a real release diff may change more surface (new CLI flags, new default adapters) than the fixtures were built against.\n\n### 9.5 Deployment\n- Ships `auto_upgrade_check: false` by default — prove on one host (ex44) for a full release cycle before flipping the fleet default, per the same \"opt-in, prove on one host first\" discipline already applied to weave/unravel/pulse. Version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, staged rollout through the canary channel (`:testing` → `:stable`), per the existing convention (§6.8/§7.3/§8.5) — this phase's own change set gets promoted through the very mechanism it's building.\n\n## Exit criteria\n- A fresh GitHub release, published while a supervisor daemon is running with `auto_upgrade_check: true`, results in every live worker on that host running the new version within one `update_check_interval_secs` + one canary cycle, with no human action required.\n- A failing canary against a release-sourced `:testing` binary leaves `:stable` untouched and the fleet running the previous version — a bad release cannot silently propagate.\n- `needle upgrade` (manual path) continues to work unchanged for fresh installs and single-host immediate upgrades.\n\n## ADR-005: 2026-07-20 — Unify the GitHub-Release Upgrade Path with the Canary-Gated Hot-Reload Channel\n\n### Context\n\nNEEDLE ships two binary-update mechanisms that share vocabulary (`:testing` / `:stable`, \"canary\", \"hot-reload\") but are structurally disconnected — confirmed by direct code read during this review, not assumption:\n\n1. **Manual GitHub-release upgrade** — `needle upgrade` (`perform_upgrade()`, `src/upgrade/mod.rs`). Downloads the latest GitHub release and `fs::rename`s it directly over `env::current_exe()` — in place, on whatever host and path the operator happens to be running it from. No canary validation. No fleet propagation: a human must run this on every host individually, and nothing does so automatically.\n2. **Self-modification canary/hot-reload channel** — `src/canary/mod.rs` plus `check_auto_canary()` / `check_hot_reload()` in `src/worker/mod.rs`. A real, implemented, unit-tested automatic pipeline: every worker's own loop, every cycle, between LOGGING and SELECTING, detects a `~/.needle/bin/needle-testing` binary, canary-validates it against `~/.needle/canary/`, promotes to `needle-stable` on an all-pass (backing up the previous stable to `needle-stable.prev` for rollback), and every live worker on that host `exec()`s into the new binary with `--resume` at its next safe loop boundary — never mid-dispatch. This works today, but is gated behind `self_modification.enabled && self_modification.auto_promote` (both `false` in the live `.needle.yaml`), and — separately from that gate — **nothing anywhere in the codebase ever writes a `needle-testing` binary from a GitHub release.** The only producer of that path today is the self-modification pipeline itself (an agent editing NEEDLE's own source and building it locally).\n\nLive evidence gathered during this audit, ex44 host, 2026-07-20: `needle --version` reported `needle 0.2.11`; GitHub's `releases/latest` API reported `v0.2.12`, `published_at: 2026-07-20T12:49:30Z` — published the same day, and never picked up by either existing path. The fleet runs up to `worker.max_workers: 10` per host across at least two hosts (ex44, lab), each worker an independent, long-lived tmux-session loop, deliberately without a central orchestrator (README: \"coordination happens through the shared bead queue\"). Any fix has to preserve that property rather than introduce a controller that pushes commands to hosts.\n\n### Decision\n\nRoute GitHub releases through the *existing* `:testing` slot instead of building a second, weaker auto-update path: add a download step (reusing `check_for_update()`'s version check) that writes a newer release to `~/.needle/bin/needle-testing`, triggered periodically from `needle supervise` (the fleet daemon that already runs continuously per host, independent of dispatch, and already owns fleet-wide operational decisions like auto-scaling) via a new `supervisor.auto_upgrade_check` flag (default `false`) and `supervisor.update_check_interval_secs` (default 6h). `check_auto_canary()` and `check_hot_reload()` — already running in every worker's loop — pick up a release-sourced `:testing` binary with zero code changes, since they only ever look at file paths and hashes, not provenance. Promotion-automatic-vs-manual continues to be governed by the existing `self_modification.auto_promote` flag rather than a new one. `needle upgrade` / `perform_upgrade()` remains available unchanged for the manual/immediate/fresh-install case. Full detail, alternatives, and evidence: [ADR-005](../adr/005-unify-release-upgrade-with-canary-hot-reload.md).\n\n### Alternatives Considered\n","numLines":200,"startLine":3998,"totalLines":4210}}}

previous_count\n            );\n        }\n\n        added_count\n    }\n\n    /// Compute the starting workspace index for this worker.\n    ///\n    /// Uses a hash of the qualified_id modulo the This de-herds workers by ensuring\n    /// they start at different positions in the workspace list.\n    ///\n    /// Returns 0 if there are no workspaces (defensive, should be handled earlier).\n    fn compute_start_index(&self) -> usize {\n        let workspaces = self.workspaces.lock().unwrap();\n        if workspaces.is_empty() {\n            return 0;\n        }\n\n        let n = workspaces.len();\n\n        // Hash the qualified_id using a stable hash algorithm\n        let mut hasher = DefaultHasher::new();\n        self.qualified_id.hash(&mut hasher);\n        let hash = hasher.finish();\n\n        // Start at hash % n, wrapping around\n        (hash as usize) % n\n    }\n\n    /// Get an iterator over workspaces in this worker's rotation order.\n    ///\n    /// The iterator starts at this worker's computed start index and wraps around,\n    /// covering all workspaces exactly once. Each worker with a different qualified_id\n    /// will visit workspaces in a different rotation.\n    fn rotated_workspace_order(&self) -> Vec<PathBuf> {\n        let workspaces = self.workspaces.lock().unwrap();\n        if workspaces.is_empty() {\n            return vec![];\n        }\n\n        let start = self.compute_start_index();\n        let n = workspaces.len();\n        let mut rotated = Vec::with_capacity(n);\n\n        // Add workspaces from start to end\n        for i in start..n {\n            rotated.push(workspaces[i].clone());\n        }\n\n        // Add workspaces from beginning to start (wrap-around)\n        for i in 0..start {\n            rotated.push(workspaces[i].clone());\n        }\n\n        rotated\n    }\n\n    /// Create a BrCliBeadStore for a given workspace path.\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    async fn store_for_workspace(workspace: &Path) -> Result<Arc<dyn BeadStore>, anyhow::Error> {\n        Ok(Arc::new(BrCliBeadStore::discover(workspace.to_path_buf())?))\n    }\n\n    /// Create a BrCliBeadStore for a given workspace path.\n    ///\n    /// This internal version is marked pub(crate) to allow testing with store injection.\n    #[cfg(test)]\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    async fn create_store_for(\n        &self,\n        workspace: &Path,\n    ) -> Result<Arc<dyn BeadStore>, anyhow::Error> {\n        self.store_factory.create_store(workspace).await\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait::async_trait]\nimpl super::Strand for ExploreStrand {\n    fn name(&self) -> &str {\n        \"explore\"\n    }\n\n    async fn evaluate(&self, _store: &dyn BeadStore) -> StrandResult {\n        use std::collections::HashSet;\n        use std::time::Instant;\n\n        // If disabled, nothing to explore.\n        if !self.enabled {\n            let _ = self\n                .telemetry\n                .emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::StrandSkipped {\n                    strand_name: \"explore\".to_string(),\n                    reason: \"disabled\".to_string(),\n                });\n            return StrandResult::NoWork;\n        }\n\n        // Increment cycle counter and check if re-discovery is due.\n        let cycles = self\n            .cycles_since_rediscovery\n            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed)\n            + 1;\n        if self.rediscovery_cycles > 0 && cycles >= self.rediscovery_cycles {\n            // Reset the counter first (in case rediscovery takes time or errors).\n            self.cycles_since_rediscovery\n                .store(0, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);\n\n            // Re-discover workspaces.\n            let added = self.rediscover_workspaces();\n            if added > 0 {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    worker = %self.qualified_id,\n                    added,\n                    \"periodic workspace re-discovery found new workspaces\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Empty workspaces (after discovery attempt) means no workspaces found.\n        {\n            let workspaces = self.workspaces.lock().unwrap();\n            if workspaces.is_empty() {\n                let _ = self\n                    .telemetry\n                    .emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::StrandSkipped {\n                        strand_name: \"explore\".to_string(),\n                        reason: \"no_workspaces_discovered\".to_string(),\n                    });\n                return StrandResult::NoWork;\n            }\n        }\n\n        let filters = Filters {\n            assignee: None,\n            exclude_labels: vec![\n                \"deferred\".to_string(),\n                \"human\".to_string(),\n                \"blocked\".to_string(),\n            ],\n        };\n\n        // Get this worker's rotated workspace order to de-herd workers\n        let workspaces = self.rotated_workspace_order();\n        let start_index = self.compute_start_index();\n\n        let total_workspaces = {\n            let workspaces = self.workspaces.lock().unwrap();\n            workspaces.len()\n        };\n\n        tracing::debug!(\n            qualified_id = %self.qualified_id,\n            total_workspaces,\n            start_index,\n            \"worker scan rotation: starting at workspace index {}\",\n            start_index\n        );\n\n        // Track scan summary information for telemetry\n        let scan_start = Instant::now();\n        let mut workspaces_visited: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        let mut workspaces_with_candidates: Vec<String> = Vec::new();\n        let mut total_candidates = 0usize;\n        let mut exclusion_reasons: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();\n\n        for workspace in &workspaces {\n            // Track this workspace as visited\n            let workspace_str = workspace.display().to_string();\n            workspaces_visited.push(workspace_str.clone());\n\n            // Skip the home workspace — Pluck already checked it.\n            if workspace == &self.home_workspace {\n                tracing::debug!(workspace = %workspace.display(), \"skipping home workspace\");\n                exclusion_reasons.insert(\"home_workspace\".to_string());\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Check that .beads/ exists before attempting to query.\n            if !Self::has_beads_dir(workspace) {\n                tracing::debug!(workspace = %workspace.display(), \"no .beads/ directory, skipping\");\n                exclusion_reasons.insert(\"no_beads_dir\".to_string());\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Create a store for this workspace and query for ready beads.\n            let remote_store = match self.store_factory.create_store(workspace).await {\n                Ok(s) => s,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        workspace = %workspace.display(),\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to create bead store for workspace, skipping\"\n                    );\n                    exclusion_reasons.insert(format!(\"store_error: {}\", e));\n                    continue;\n                }\n            };\n\n            match remote_store.ready(&filters).await {\n                Ok(mut candidates) => {\n                    // Defensive belt-and-suspenders filtering.\n                    // The store.ready() method receives exclude_labels in its Filters,\n                    // but some backend implementations may not filter correctly.\n                    // This ensures excluded/assigned beads are never returned as candidates.\n                    let before_count = candidates.len();\n                    candidates.retain(|b| {\n                        let assignee_ok = b.assignee.is_none();\n                        let labels_ok =\n                            !b.labels.iter().any(|l| filters.exclude_labels.contains(l));\n                        assignee_ok && labels_ok\n                    });\n                    let filtered_count = before_count - candidates.len();\n\n                    if filtered_count > 0 {\n                        exclusion_reasons.insert(format!(\"filtered_{}\", filtered_count));\n                    }\n\n                    if candidates.is_empty() {\n                        // No ready candidates. Run cross-workspace mend to release\n                        // orphaned in-progress beads, then re-query.\n                        tracing::debug!(\n                            workspace = %workspace.display(),\n                            \"no ready candidates, running cross-workspace mend\"\n                        );\n                        exclusion_reasons.insert(\"no_ready_candidates\".to_string());\n\n                        match super::cleanup_orphaned_in_progress(\n                            remote_store.as_ref(),\n                            &self.registry,\n                            &self.telemetry,\n                            &self.qualified_id,\n                        )\n                        .await\n                        {\n                            Ok(released) if released > 0 => {\n                                tracing::info!(\n                                    workspace = %workspace.display(),\n                                    released,\n                                    \"cross-workspace mend released orphans, re-querying\"\n                                );\n\n                                // Re-query ready after cleanup.\n                                match remote_store.ready(&filters).await {\n                                    Ok(mut retry_candidates) => {\n                                        // Apply the same defensive filtering.\n                                        let retry_before = retry_candidates.len();\n                                        retry_candidates.retain(|b| {\n                                            let assignee_ok = b.assignee.is_none();\n                                            let labels_ok = !b\n                                                .labels\n                                                .iter()\n                                                .any(|l| filters.exclude_labels.contains(l));\n                                            assignee_ok && labels_ok\n                                        });\n                                        let retry_filtered = retry_before - retry_candidates.len();\n\n                                        if retry_filtered > 0 {\n                                            exclusion_reasons.insert(format!(\n                                                \"retry_filtered_{}\",\n                                                retry_filtered\n                                            ));\n                                        }\n\n                                        if !retry_candidates.is_empty() {\n                                            // Found candidates after releasing orphans.\n                                            // Sort and tag them.\n                                            retry_candidates.sort_by(|a, b| {\n                                                a.priority\n                                                    .cmp(&b.priority)\n                                                    .then_with(|| a.created_at.cmp(&b.created_at))\n                                                    .then_with(|| a.id.as_ref().cmp(b.id.as_ref()))\n                                            });\n\n                                            for bead in &mut retry_candidates {\n                                                bead.workspace = workspace.clone();\n                                            }\n\n                                            // Track scan results before returning\n                                            workspaces_with_candidates.push(workspace_str);\n                                            total_candidates += retry_candidates.len();\n                                            let duration_ms =\n                                                scan_start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;\n                                            let _ = self.telemetry.emit(\n                                                crate::telemetry::EventKind::ExploreScanSummary {\n                                                    workspaces_visited,\n                                                    workspaces_with_candidates,\n                                                    total_candidates,\n                                                    exclusion_reasons: exclusion_reasons\n                                                        .into_iter()\n                                                        .collect(),\n                                                    duration_ms,\n                                                },\n                                            );\n\n                                            tracing::info!(\n                                                workspace = %workspace.display(),\n                                                candidates = retry_candidates.len(),\n                                                \"explore found candidates in remote workspace after cross-workspace mend\"\n                                            );\n\n                                            return StrandResult::BeadFound(retry_candidates);\n                                        }\n\n                                        // Orphans were released but re-query found no candidates.\n                                        // Do NOT return WorkCreated — the beads will become available\n                                        // in the next natural selection cycle when Pluck re-scans the\n                                        // ready queue. Returning WorkCreated here causes restart loops\n                                        // when released beads don't pass filters (e.g., still blocked).\n                                        tracing::info!(\n                                            workspace = %workspace.display(),\n                                            released,\n                                            \"cross-workspace mend released orphans but re-query found no candidates (beads may not pass filters), continuing to next workspace\"\n                                        );\n                                        exclusion_reasons\n                                            .insert(\"orphans_released_no_candidates\".to_string());\n                                    }\n                                    Err(e) => {\n                                        tracing::warn!(\n                                            workspace = %workspace.display(),\n                                            error = %e,\n                                            \"failed to re-query workspace after cross-workspace mend, skipping\"\n                                        );\n                                        exclusion_reasons.insert(format!(\"requery_error: {}\", e));\n                                    }\n                                }\n                            }\n                            Ok(_) => {\n                                // No orphans released, workspace is truly empty.\n                                tracing::debug!(\n                                    workspace exclusion_reasons.insert(\"no_orphans\".to_string());\n                            }\n                            Err(e) => {\n                                tracing::warn!(\n                                    workspace = %workspace.display(),\n                                    error = %e,\n                                    \"cross-workspace mend failed, skipping workspace\"\n                                );\n                                exclusion_reasons.insert(format!(\"mend_error: {}\", e));\n                            }\n                        }\n\n                        // Advance to next workspace (candidates empty after mend).\n                        continue;\n                    }\n\n                    // Sort deterministically: priority ASC, created_at ASC, id ASC.\n                    candidates.sort_by(|a, b| {\n                        a.priority\n                            .cmp(&b.priority)\n                            .then_with(|| a.created_at.cmp(&b.created_at))\n                            .then_with(|| a.id.as_ref().cmp(b.id.as_ref()))\n                    });\n\n                    // Tag each candidate with the workspace it came from\n                    // so the worker can create the correct bead store.\n                    for bead in &mut candidates {\n                        bead.workspace = workspace.clone();\n                    }\n\n                    // Track successful workspace scan\n                    workspaces_with_candidates.push(workspace_str);\n                    total_candidates += candidates.len();\n                    let duration_ms = scan_start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;\n\n                    let _ = self\n                        .telemetry\n                        .emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::ExploreScanSummary {\n                            workspaces_visited,\n                            workspaces_with_candidates,\n                            total_candidates,\n                            exclusion_reasons: exclusion_reasons.into_iter().collect(),\n                            duration_ms,\n                        });\n\n                    tracing::info!(\n                        workspace = %workspace.display(),\n                        candidates = candidates.len(),\n                        \"explore found candidates in remote workspace\"\n                    );\n\n                    return StrandResult::BeadFound(candidates);\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        workspace = %workspace.display(),\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to query workspace, skipping\"\n                    );\n                    exclusion_reasons.insert(format!(\"query_error: {}\", e));\n                    continue;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // No candidates found in any workspace - emit scan
